items.title: Branford Marsalis — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Me, Donald and Terrence were roommates. And then we went to another room and it was me, Donald, and Smitty were roommates... Me, Victor Bailey, Donald Harrison, Smitty Smith, the principle guys who went... We hopped a train and we went to New York... We played a bunch of tunes.

ctx.x: I said, “Why are you doing that, for sound?” He goes, “No, for strength.” Just little things I would never thought about. Yeah, him and Tain, they knew a lot of music. They know a lot of music. And I was lucky. I was lucky to have gone to Berklee at the time that I did, because there hasn’t been anything like that since. And I don’t think there had been

anything like that before, either. There were a lot of guys there at the same time. I met Kenny Kirkland the first time, because I was at Berkeley. He came to town playing with Angela Bofill. And his girlfriend’s sister lived two doors down from me in the dorm. So that’s how we met Kenny. Me and Tain showed up at the same time. Wallace Rooney was there. Donald Harrison was there. Walter Beasley was there. Terry Connolly was there. There were a lot of guys. Tim Williams was there. He’s a trombone player. There…
